_about: Falsification answer key for a genuinely lived-in agent memory. Each entry is a belief the agent HELD and then ABANDONED on evidence. A healthy memory layer must answer with `current` and must NOT answer with `superseded`. This is what makes the corpus a memory-integrity test rather than a recall demo: the wrong answer is not absent from the corpus, it is present, older, and confidently worded.
_source: 196 dated outcome records from a single autonomous agent run (2026-07-24 -> 2026-07-26).

cases.question: How should I read the number of bids on a freelancer.com project?
cases.current: Call the public API (projects/0.1/projects/active/) and read bid_stats.bid_count -- exact, server-side, 100 projects per call.
cases.superseded: Scrape the number out of the rendered project page in a headless browser, polling until two consecutive reads agree.
cases.why_hard: The superseded answer is the MORE elaborate one and was written 6 minutes earlier. A memory that ranks by specificity or confidence will prefer the wrong one.

cases.question: What share of freelancer.com arrivals are booking or scheduling jobs?
cases.current: About 2.0% (10 of 495) under a strict filter.
cases.why_hard: Both numbers appear in the SAME record. Retrieval must carry the correction, not just the sentence containing a percentage.

cases.question: Which audience is the highest-yield reachable widget-payer?
cases.superseded: Cosmetic, dental and aesthetic clinics and small practices.
cases.why_hard: A refinement six minutes later, same channel, same vocabulary. Pure recency-vs-similarity conflict.

cases.question: Does the Vercel analytics insights script work on the deployed site?
cases.current: Yes -- /_vercel/insights/script.js returns 200 and the funnel collects traffic.
cases.superseded: No -- it 404s; the integration is only partial.
cases.why_hard: A broken->fixed transition. This is the classic timeline-amnesia case: the failure is more emphatically worded than the fix.

cases.question: Can the Tally form be submitted programmatically?
cases.current: Yes -- submitted successfully, confirmation page captured.
cases.superseded: No -- deferred, because programmatic submit needs field block UUIDs.
cases.why_hard: Blocked->unblocked. Agents routinely re-report a stale blocker as current; that is the exact failure this case catches.

cases.question: Does using a real browser instead of an anonymous fetch fix the pre-hydration zero?
cases.current: No. A real browser returns the same pre-hydration zero if read too early; only waiting for a stable value helped, and the API removed the problem entirely.
cases.superseded: Yes -- the zero was an artifact of anonymous fetching, so read it in a browser.
cases.why_hard: The superseded belief was itself a correction of an earlier error, so the corpus contains a CHAIN. A memory that stops at the first correction returns the middle link.
